<entry id="S00202">
<head-word>קֵהֶה</head-word>
<head-word>קֵי'</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, קֵהָה, קֵי' f. (preced.; cmp. כֵּהֶה) 
<italic>dull, faint</italic>; </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (of cutting tools) 
<italic>blunt</italic>; (of teeth) 
<italic>blunt and loose.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—</italic>
<plural-form>Pl. קֵהִים, קֵהִין, קֵי'; קֵהוֹת, קֵי'</plural-form>. Midr. Sam. ch. XVI as with the grape vine כל מי … שיניו ק' וכ' he that eats of its unripe fruit, will have his teeth set on edge, so it is with Israel &c.; Lev. R. s. 36 (corr. version after Midr. Sam.).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (of limbs) 
<italic>wearied, benumbed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Yoma VIII, 44
<sup>d</sup> בבא מן … ק' עליו in the case of one that had come from a journey, and his feet were benumbed; Y. Ber. II, 5
<sup>b</sup> bot.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>tough, hard, unyielding</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Taan. 7
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Koh. X, 10) אם ראית רקיע שק' כברזל וכ' when thou seest the sky as tough as iron not sending down dew or rain; Yalk. Koh. 979 אם … דור שהשמים קהין וכ' when thou seest a generation over which the heavens are as tough &c. Ab. IV, 20 ענבים קהות hard (unripe) grapes, opp. בשולות.—Trnsf. (of intellectual subjects) 
<italic>tough, difficult, unsolvable</italic>. Yalk. l. c. אם … שתלמודו ק' עליו כברזל when thou seest a student to whom his lesson is as tough as iron (Taan. 8
<sup>a</sup> שלמודו קשה; Ms. M. כהה). Pesik. R. s. 33 והמעשה שהיה ק' וכ' and when a case was too difficult for me to decide, I asked &c.; Yalk. Job 917. Cant. R. to IV, 11; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>fainting, having a morbid appetite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shebi. IV, end, 35
<sup>c</sup> שכן דרך הק' אוכלות אותו for craving women are in the habit of eating it (the unripe grape).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00203">
<head-word>קהי</head-word>
<head-word>קָהָה</head-word>
<head-word>קָהָא</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. כָּהָה)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be dull, blunt</italic>; (of a sword) 
<italic>to slide off a hard object</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. IX, 13
<sup>a</sup> וקָהַת החרב מעל וכ' and the sword slid off Moses’ neck and broke; Deut. R. s. 2; Yalk. Ex. 167 וקהית (corr. acc.). Gen. R. s. 78; Cant. R. to VII, 5 וקָהוּ שיניו וכ' and the teeth of the wicked (Esau) became blunt and loose.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be tough, unyielding, hard</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 3 (ref. to Koh. X, 10) אם ראית שקהו השמים וכ', v. preced.—Trnsf. 
<italic>to be difficult, unsolvable</italic>. Cant. R. to III, 7 שהיו כולן שונין … הלכה קוֹהָא להם they all sharpened the discussion like a sword, so that, when a case came before them, the decision might not be too difficult for them. Ib. to IV, 4 שאין הלכה קוהא להם never was there a subject too difficult for them to decide; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be wearied; to faint</italic>; esp. 
<italic>to have a morbid appetite</italic> (caused by the smell of a dish).</definition>
<notes> Ib. to I, 12 the Lord sent them a sweet scent from Eden והיתה נפשם קוהא לאכול and they were dying to eat (of the Passover sacrifice), v. עָיֵף; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְהָה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (with שן) 
<italic>to make blunt and loose</italic>; trnsf. 
<italic>to refute; to break the power of; to grieve</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Bo, s. 18 אף אתה הַקְהֵה את שיניו thou, too, make his teeth blunt (refute his arguments). Gen. R. s. 99 (play on יקהת, Gen. XLIX, 10) מי שמַקְהֶה שני וכ' he (the Messiah) that shall break the power of all nations; ib. s. 98. Sot. 49
<sup>a</sup> [read:] אומרים … למה הִקְהִיתָ וכ' (v. Rashi) they (the children of the wicked that died in their parents’ lifetime) argue before him, … if thou intendedst to punish them in the hereafter, why didst thou cause them grief while living? Ib. שמחת … והקהית השיני thou hast gladdened 
<pgbrk id="pg1322" />my heart (with the evidence of thy purity) and given me pain (by showing more affection for thy son than for myself). Snh. 109
<sup>b</sup> (play on בן קהת, Num. XVI, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> בן שה' וכ' a son that brought grief over his parents; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קֵיהָה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to pronounce unsolvable</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Neg. IV, 11, v. כָּהָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִקְהָה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become faint, powerless</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Koh. R. to X, 10 אם נִקְהֵת אומה וכ' if the nation whose power was as hard as iron, has grown powerless.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be tough, difficult</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. אם נ' תלמודך וכ' if thy lesson is as tough to thee as iron (v. preced).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקָהֵא, הִתְקָהֶה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>; 
<italic>Nithpa.</italic> נִתְקָהֶה </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to faint, long for</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Ex. 186 (ref. to מתלקחת, Ex. IX, 24) מִתְקָהָא לעשות שליחותה (not שליחותיה) it (the fire) was dying to perform its mission; Pesik. Vayhi, p. 4
<sup>a</sup> מיתה מתקהא וכ' Ar. (ed. מתקריא, corr. acc.) dying, that is longing &c.; Cant. R. to III, 11 מיתה ומתקלהא בשביל לעשות רצון בוראם (corr. acc., a. read בוראה); Num. R. s. 12 (combining both versions) מיתה ומתקהלא לעשות … בוראה (corr. acc.).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become tough, hard, unyielding, grievous, irksome</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Koh. R. l. c. אם נִתְקָהוּ שמים שעל וכ' if the heavens above you have become hard as iron &c., v. supra. Ib. אם נתק' הרב על התלמיד וכ' if the teacher has been unyielding to the pupil like iron (out of patience, and refusing to teach him) …, and the teacher shows not a friendly face (does not relent) &c. Ib. אם נתק' התלמיד על הרב וכ' if the pupil has been annoying to his teacher (through his obtuseness or wearisome questions) …, and the teacher refuses to explain &c.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00204">
<head-word>קְהֵי</head-word>
<head-word>קְהִא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be blunt</italic> (
<italic>and loose</italic>); 
<italic>to be dull, faint</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. II Gen. XXXIII, 4 (Y. I אתמזמיזו). Ib. XXXII, 26 וקהת (some ed. וקחת, v. קְחַח; Y. I זעזע; h. text ותקע).—[Targ. I Kings XIV, 4 קהאה (ed. Wil. כהאה; ed. Lag. קמא; h. text קמו.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be stale, distasteful</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 56
<sup>a</sup> קהא עסקך וכ' Ms. F. (ed. קָאוֵי fr. קְוָא; Ms. M. פסיד עסקך וקאזיל, read וקאוי) thy business (wine store) will be stale (and taste) like a pomegranate.—Part. pass. קְהִיהַ, 
<italic>pl</italic>. קְהִיתִין (cmp. חֲמִי, a. חַמְת'). Lev. R. s. 19 הא קהיתין are they (the vessels with wine you have been examining) spoiled?; [Ar. s. v. קה: הָקְהֵיתָה is it spoiled?].</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be unrelenting, rigorous</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. 52
<sup>b</sup> דקָהֵי אזוזי מקרי נפש רעה Ar. (ed. דמוקים) he who is rigorous in matters of coins (refusing a coin for slight imperfections) is called ‘a malevolent soul’ (v. נֶפֶשׁ).</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קַהֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to give an acrid taste to</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 116
<sup>a</sup> צריך לְקַהוּיֵיה one must give the pap (חֲרוֹסֶת) an acrid taste (with apples and wine).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַקְהֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>to blunt a person’s teeth</italic>,] 
<italic>to refute, argue</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 110
<sup>b</sup> מַקְהוּ Ar. a. Var. in Rashi (ed. מַקְווּ), v. אַקְוָוא.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00205">
<head-word>קַהֲיוּת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>

<italic>bluntness of teeth</italic>; trnsf. 
<italic>old age</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Lam. 996 בן שנתן לו בק' ש' וכ' the son that was given him (Abraham) in his old age, when he was one hundred years old.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00208">
<head-word>קָהַל</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. קוֹל)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to call</italic>.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְהִיל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to assemble</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 61
<sup>b</sup>; Ab. Zar. 18
<sup>a</sup> מַקְהִיל קהילות ברבים called public assemblies (to teach). Gen. R. s. 99 כשיַקְהִיל קרח וכ' (some ed. כשיַקְהֵל) when Korah will gather his followers for strife, my (Jacob’s) name shall not be joined with them. Yalk. Ex. 408 כדי שילמדו … להַקְהִיל וכ' that coming generations may learn from thee to assemble congregations every Sabbath; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִקְהַל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be assembled</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 98 בשעה שהן נִקְהָלִין על וכ' when they will be assembled against Moses in the party of Korah &c. Lev. R. s. 24 פרשה … בהִקָּהֵל וכ' this section (Lev. XIX) was proclaimed in full assembly (v. ib. 2), because &c. Koh. R. to I, 1, v. קֹהֶלֶת.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקָהֵל</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> same. Gen. R. s. 99 (ref. to יקהת, Gen. XLIX, 10) מי … מִתְקָהֲלִין עליו he around whom the nations will group themselves.—[Num. R. s. 12 מתקהלא, v. קָהָה.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00209">
<head-word>קָהָל</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) 
<italic>gathering, congregation</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Hor. I, 46
<sup>a</sup> bot. (ref. to Num. XV, 24, העדה) כל השבטים קרויין ק' all tribes together are called 
<italic>ḳahal</italic>; כל שבט … ק' every tribe for itself is called ḳ.; Bab. ib. 3
<sup>a</sup> כגון … רובו של ק' וכ' when six tribes have sinned, and they form the majority of the congregation (the entire people) &c. Ib. הני הוא דאיקרו ק' only they (the entire people) are called 
<italic>ḳ</italic>.—Kidd. 73
<sup>a</sup> קְהַל ודאי a community of Israelites of undoubted legitimacy; קְ' ספק of doubtful legitimacy; Y. Yeb. VIII, 9
<sup>b</sup> bot. קָ' ברור; קְ' ספק. Ib. [read:] ארבע קְהִילּוֹת אינון קְ' יי' קְ' כהנים וכ' four communities are meant by ‘the congregation of the Lord’ (Deut. XXIII, 2; 3; 4; 9): the community of priests, of Levites, of Israelites, and of proselytes. Mish. ib. VIII, 2 ואינן … אלא מלבא בק' and they are forbidden only to enter the congregation (to intermarry with Israelites); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl., v. קְהִלָּה</plural-form></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00210">
<head-word>קָהָל</head-word>
<head-word>קַהֲלָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same.</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Targ. Num. XVI, 3. Ib. XX, 4; a. fr.—Kidd. 73
<sup>a</sup> מחד קהל נפקו ed. (Rashi קהלא) the (laws concerning priests and Levites) are derived from one of the verses (Deut. XXIII, 3; 4; 9) in which 
<italic>ḳahal</italic> occurs.—
<plural-form>Pl. קַהֲלֵי</plural-form>. Ib. הנהו נמי תרי ק' נינהו these (priests and Levites) are also two communities (requiring two verses with the word 
<italic>ḳahal</italic> in them); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00211">
<head-word>קְהִלָּה</head-word>
<head-word>קְהִי'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) same.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. VII, 11
<sup>c</sup> top במקהלות כל ק' וק' ‘in assemblies praise God’ (Ps. LXVIII, 27), in every kind of assemblies (use a different phraseology for the appeal to praise God, according to the size of the assembly). Meg. 2
<sup>a</sup> י"ג זמן ק' וכ' the thirteenth of Adar was the date of gathering all Jews (Esth. IX, 18). Lev. R. s. 9 (ref. to Deut. XXXIII, 4) מורשה קְהִלַּת ינאי אין וכ' it is not written here, ‘an inheritance of the congregation of Yannai’ (privileged scholars), but of the congregation of Jacob (v. יְרוּתָּא); a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. קְהִלּוֹת, קְהִי'</plural-form>. Y. Yeb, VIII, 9
<sup>b</sup> bot., v. קָהָל. Ab. Zar. 18
<sup>a</sup>, a. e., v. קָהַל; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00212">
<head-word>קֹהֶלֶת</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.)
<pos> pr. n. m.</pos>
<italic>Koheleth</italic>, traditional surname of King Solomon.</definition>
<notes> Koh. R. to I, 1 למה נקרא שמו ק' … בהִקָּהֵל וכ' why was his name Koheleth? Because his words were proclaimed in public meeting, as it is written (I Kings VIII, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> &c.; a. e.—ק' (ספר) 
<italic>the Book of Koheleth</italic>, 
<pgbrk id="pg1323" />
<italic>Ecclesiastes</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 14
<sup>b</sup> סידרן … ק' וכ' the order of the books of Hagiographa is: Ruth, Psalms, Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes &c. Ib. 15
<sup>a</sup> משלי … ק' אנשי וכ' the men of the Great Assembly composed Proverbs, Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes. Sabb. 30
<sup>b</sup> בקשו … ספר ק' וכ' the scholars wanted to exclude from the canon (v. גָּנַז) the book of E., because its words contradict one another; Koh. R. to I, 3; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00213">
<head-word>קָהַרְמָנָא</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Pers. 
<italic>Ḳaharmân</italic>) 
<italic>administrator, curator</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 46
<sup>b</sup> ק' שוויה Ar. (read: שויוהו; v. הַרְמנְיָא) they made him an administrator (of their property, and as such he let it out to tenants). Erub. 59
<sup>a</sup> דשכיחי גבי ק' Ar. (ed. הרמנא) they are accustomed to meet at the office of the curator of the city, v. הַרְמָנָא.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00215">
<head-word>קַו</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> v. 
<xref rid="S00308">קָוָה</xref>) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>circle, zone</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥag. 12
<sup>a</sup> תהו קו ירוק וכ' 
<italic>tohu</italic> (Gen. I, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> is the green (or yellow) circle which surrounds the whole world (the horizon); Yalk. Kings 185 (ref. to I Kings VII, 23) זה קו ירוק וכ' this is typical of the green circle &c. Num. R. s. 13 קו הים שעשה וכ' the circle encompassing the basin which Solomon made (I Kings l. c.); a. e.— [
<italic>cavity</italic>,] 
<italic>the lower part of a trumpet</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kel. XI, 7, v. קב.—[Tanḥ. Aḥăré 1 קו שררתיה, v. קוֹשַׁרְתָּא.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00216">
<head-word>קַיָּא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>(preced., v. P. Sm. 3510; cmp. כַּוָּא) [

<italic>web.</italic></definition>

<entry id="S00217">
<head-word>קוּא</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to spit</italic>.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הֵקִיא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>

<sup>a</sup> נוהגין אותו היום ק' וכ' we observe the rest of the day as a holy day and the next day likewise. Pes. 104
<sup>a</sup>; Ḥull. 26
<sup>a</sup>, v. חוֹל III. Ib. I, 7 בין ק' לק', v. בָּדַל; ib. בין ק' חמוד לק' הקל between the stricter and the lighter sanctities; a. v. fr.—שם ק' or ק' (sub. שם) sacred name, name of the Lord. Shebu. 35
<sup>b</sup>, v. חוֹל III. Treat. Sof’rim IV, 6, sq.; a. fr.—רוח הק', v. רוּחַ.—Esp. 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>sacred precincts, Temple ground</italic>. Zeb. IX, 2 כל שפסולו בק' הק' מקבלו whatever has become unfit within the sanctuary, the sanctuary accepts (it cannot be removed from the altar, if it was put on); לא היה פסולו בק' וכ' if its unfitness did not arise within the sacred precincts, the sanctuary does not accept it; a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) הק' 
<italic>the Holy</italic>, contrad. to עֲזָרָה, a. to ק' הקדשים, v. infra. Yoma III, 3; 6 בק' within the precincts of the Holy. Midd. IV, 5; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קֳדָשִׁים</plural-form>.—קודש הק', also קָדְשֵׁי ק' 
<italic>most holy</italic>, esp. 
<italic>the Holy of Holies</italic>, the westernmost compartment of the Temple. Midd. l. c. Yoma V, 1; a. fr.—Cant. R. to I, 1 כל הכתובים קדש וזה ק' הק' all Biblical scriptures are holy, but this (Song of Songs) is most holy. Y. Meg. III, 74
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. נחום איש קדש הק' Nahum, the man of extreme holiness; a. e.—Esp. קֳדָשִׁים 
<italic>consecrated objects, sacrifices</italic>. Zeb. V, 4 העולה קדשי ק' the burnt-offering belongs to the highest class of sacrifices. Ib. 6, sq. ק' קלים sacrifices of a minor grade. Ib. III, 35, with allusion to וירם תולעים, Ex. XVI, 20) היתה ק̇ל̇אנ̇ין של תולעים וכי a night watch of vermin (that keep people awake) went forth &c.; Y’lamd. to Ex. XXVIII quot. in Ar. קלנין; (Yalk. <senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to stand up, rise; to stand, exist</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifré Deut. 357 (ref. to Deut. XXXIV, 10) אבל באומות קָם וכ' but among the nations he (a prophet like Moses) has existed &c.; R. Hash. 21
<sup>b</sup> בנביאים לא קם וכ' among the prophets never one arose like Moses, but among the rulers one did arise (Solomon). Tanḥ. B’shall. 16 שכל הַקָּם … כאילו קם וכ' whoever rises against Israel is considered as if he rose against the Sh’khinah. Ib. (ref. to Ex. XV, 7) הרבית … כל הקָּמִים לנגדך thou hast often shown thyself glorious over all that rose against thee; a. v. fr.—קוּם עֲשֵׂה rise and do, 
<italic>a transgression of a prohibitive law which you must repair by an action</italic>, v. נָתַק. Ḥull. XII, 4. Macc. 15
<sup>b</sup>, v. infra; a. fr.—V. קַיָּים.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִיֵּים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to establish; to attest, identify</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 2
<sup>b</sup> אין עדים מצויין לקַיְּימוֹ no witnesses are likely to be found to attest it (identify the signatures). Ib. 6
<sup>a</sup> כולי עלמא בעינן לקיימו all agree that identifiation by witnesses is required. B. Mets. 7
<sup>a</sup> מודה בשטר … צריך לקיימו even if the debtor admits that he has written the note, the creditor must establish its identity (or else the debtor may maintain that the debt has been paid). Gitt. III, 4 וקיְּימוּ את דבריו and they sustained his opinion. Keth. 20
<sup>a</sup> אין מְקַיְּימִין … אלא משטר וכ' a document can be identified only by comparison of the signatures with those on a document that had been disputed and declared valid in court. Ib. אין מקיימין … משתי כתובות וכ' a document can be identified only by comparison of signatures with two marriage deeds or deeds of sale of two fields &c. Ned. 72
<sup>a</sup> שמע וק' if he heard her vow and confirmed it. Y. R. Hash. I, 56
<sup>c</sup> top קִיַּימְתִּיהָ כשחל וכ' I sustain that opinion for a case when &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְקוּיָּים. B. Mets. l. c. במק' דברי וכ' if the document has been identified, all agree &c.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to fulfill, carry out, execute</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yoma 28
<sup>b</sup> ק' אברהם וכ' Abraham fulfilled the whole Law. Macc. l. c. כל מצות … ק' וכ' in the case of a transgression of a prohibitive law for which reparation is commanded, if the transgressor fulfills the prescribed reparation, he is free (from legal punishment), but if he made the reparation impossible &c. Ib. ור"ש בן ל' קִיְּימוֹ ולא קִיְּימוֹ R. S. ben L. reads, if he makes reparation (he is free), and if he refuses, (he is punished); ib. 15
<sup>a</sup> למאן דאמר ק' ולא ק' according to him who reads 
<italic>ḳiyy’mo v’lo ḳiyy’mo</italic> (punishment can be executed as soon as one refuses to make reparation, although reparation is not made impossible); Ḥull. 141
<sup>a</sup>. Ab. IV, 9 כל הַמְקַיֵּים … לקַיְּימָהּ מעושר he who maintains (studies and observes) the Law in poverty, shall finally maintain it in wealth. Sot. 13
<sup>a</sup> sq. אמרו ק' זה כל וכ' they said, this one (Joseph in the coffin) has fulfilled what is written in this (the tablets in the ark of the covenant). Y. R. Hash. I, 57
<sup>b</sup> top רצה מְקַיְּימָהּ if he so desires, he observes it (his own decree). Ber. 9
<sup>b</sup> ועבדום … ק' בהם וכ' the Lord fulfilled on them ‘and they shall make them serve &c.’ (Gen. XV, 14), but he did not fulfill on them &c.; a. v. fr.—מה אני מקיים וכ' how can I maintain the words &c., i.e. in what way can this Scriptural verse which seems to conflict with my opinion be interpreted? R. Hash. 21
<sup>b</sup> אלא מה אני מקיים ביקש וכ' and how do I interpret the verse 
<italic>biḳḳesh</italic> &c. (Koh. XII, 10)? Y. Kidd. I, 61
<sup>c</sup> bot. מה מקיים … בנים how does R. Elazar interpret 
<italic>banim</italic> &c. (Deut. XIV, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to sustain, preserve alive, save</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. IV, 5 כל המקיים … כאילו ק' וכ' he who saves one life … is considered … as if he had preserved the whole world; B. Bath. 11
<sup>a</sup>. Ab. V, 1 צדיקים שמקיימין את העילם וכ' the righteous who sustain the world which was created &c. Kil. V, 8 המקיים קוצים בכרם he who keeps (cultivates) thorns in a vineyard. Ib. דבר שכמוהו מקיימין a plant of the kind that people are wont to cultivate; a. e.—4) 
<italic>to place</italic> (
<italic>on the chafing stove</italic>). Tosef. Sabb. III, 1 ואין מקיימין עליה וכ' (not לה) you must not place dishes on it, until it is swept or covered with ashes. Ib. 3; Y. ib. III, beg. 5
<sup>c</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקַיֵּים, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְקַיֵּים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be established, identified</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. I, 3 יִתְקַיֵּים בחותמיו let the genuineness of the document be established through its signers (the witnesses subscribed or through others identifying their signatures); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be fulfilled, realized</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. 24
<sup>b</sup> עד שלא נִתְקַיְּימָה … שלא תִתְקַיֵּים נבואתו וכ' as long as the prophecy of Uriah (Mic. III, 12) was not fulfilled, I was afraid lest Zechariah’s prophecy (Zech. VIII, 4) fail to come true; עכשיו שנתקיימה … מִתְקַיֶּימֶת now that Uriah’s prophecy has been fulfilled, it is sure that Zechariah’s will come true. Tosef. Snh. XI, 8; Y. ib. XI, 30
<sup>a</sup> bot. וכולן נִתְקַיְּימוּ, v. מִדָּה. Ber. 55
<sup>a</sup> מקצתו מתקיים וכ' part of a dream may come true, but the whole of it will not. Midr. Till. to Ps. I, 3 מִתְקַיְּימוֹת are executed, v. עֵצָה II; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be preserved; to last, endure</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. II, 3 בכל דבר שאינו מתקיים with any writing-ink which does not endure. Pes. 68
<sup>b</sup>
<pgbrk id="pg1331" />אילמלא … לא נתקיימו וכ' but for the Law, heaven and earth would not continue to exist. Taan. 7
<sup>a</sup> מה … מִתְקַיְּימִין וכ' as these three liquids can be preserved only in the lowest kind of vessels, so will the words of the Law stay with him only whose mind is lowly. Erub. 54
<sup>a</sup> תלמודו מתק' בידו his learning will remain with him (in his memory). Shebi. VII, 2 מתק' בארץ plants the roots of which continue in the ground (perennials). Ab. IV, 11 כל כנסיה … סופה להִתְקַיֵּים every union for a sacred purpose is destined to last. Ib. V, 17 כל מחלוקת … סופה להתק' a contest for a sacred purpose is bound to have an enduring effect; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be maintained, be harmonised</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Mishp. s. 20 כיצד יִתְקַיְּימוּ שני מקראות הללו how can these two verses be harmonised?; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<sup>a</sup> (corr. acc.). Y. Ter. I, 40
<sup>b</sup> top בחרש אנן קָיְימִין we are standing at (are treating of) the case of a deaf mute. Y. Maasr. I, 51
